project.title: Snake
project.description: Classic-inspired Snake on a PRG32 tile playfield: eat apples, grow, avoid walls and your tail.
project.author: PRG32 Kit

fields.TEXT: Snake: eat the apples, avoid the walls and your own tail.
Tile 0 is the empty floor. Defining it keeps every PRG32 runtime drawing it the same way.
Tiles 1-4: wall, body, head and apple, each an 8 x 8 picture with two colours.
New board: clear the playfield, then put wall tiles (1) all around it.
The body is a ring buffer: head is the newest cell, length cells back is the tail.
Try random cells until an empty one is found.
Mode 0 = title, 1 = playing, 2 = game over.
New board: clear the playfield, then put wall tiles (1) all around it.
The body is a ring buffer: head is the newest cell, length cells back is the tail.
Try random cells until an empty one is found.
Playing: steer, then move one cell at a time.
Turning is allowed only sideways: the snake cannot reverse into itself.
The snake moves one cell every 'speed' frames.
Look at the tile in front of the head: a wall or the body ends the game.
Move: the old head becomes body, the new head is stored and drawn.
An apple makes the snake longer; otherwise the tail cell is erased.
Try random cells until an empty one is found.
Show the score in the PRG32 status band.
SCORE
One block draws the whole board: 40 x 25 tiles of playfield layer 0.
Text is drawn on top of the tiles.
